# Running the Design Loop {#sec-running-the-loop}

::: {.callout-crux}
What can an architect conclude when the declared Lighthouse cache study cannot
run and a separate retained array study also stops short of the system goal?
:::

Running a design loop means carrying a fixed architecture question through
candidate selection, tool execution, measurement, interpretation, and a
supported stopping decision. This chapter makes that sequence concrete with
two complementary records. They teach different parts of the work and are not
combined into one end-to-end result.

The first record follows the Lighthouse goal for a low-power, 64-bit
RISC-V-based compute subsystem for a real-time mobile extended reality (XR)
workload. It narrows that system goal to one pre-RTL cache-capacity decision
named `XR-L2-CAP-A`. The declaration identifies the candidates, controlled
design fields, planned tools, returns, checks, call-count limits, and intended
decision. It also exposes work required before execution. The prospective study
specification must bind the cache-policy fields and capacity-derived structure,
complete the decision procedure, define numeric deadlines and cost accounting,
materialize the candidate artifacts, translate them into executable requests,
bind the placeholder names to executable tools, and provide a retained
measurement path.

The prospective cache study was therefore not run. No cache number, failure,
retry, dispatch, return, or cost in the author-constructed teaching records is
measured project evidence. The larger cache candidates remain unevaluated, the
baseline remains unrerun, and the pre-RTL decision remains open. This is the
supported outcome of the Lighthouse path.

The second record is a separate systolic-array study with retained inputs and
SCALE-Sim outputs. Its twelve simulator evaluation events show the operational
sequence after execution becomes possible: compare candidates, test the
proposed mechanism, inspect omitted quantities, record the available runtime
and model-usage costs, expose the missing cost fields, and decide where to
stop. The result is a tie against a fixed heuristic, a failed directional
explanation, incomplete provenance, and no authorized acceptance or rejection.
It cannot complete the cache study, validate the 3\ W subsystem
target, or stand in for the Lighthouse system. Neither record is a complete
Lighthouse success.

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}
After reading this chapter, you can:

- Trace an architecture question through fixed state, execution, returned
  measurements, interpretation, and a supported stop.
- Distinguish a prospective study and teaching fixtures from retained execution
  evidence.
- Separate the architecture outcome, method contribution, mechanism result,
  and next action supported by a run.
- Use ties, failed explanations, omitted metrics, and provenance gaps to define
  a better follow-up study.

:::

## Preparing a Cache Study That Could Run

The cache case first defines the architecture decision and then asks what must
exist before that decision can be evaluated. This order matters. A runnable
tool path is useful only after the candidates, controlled design fields, checks,
and permitted conclusion are clear. The resulting declaration exposes the work
still required without manufacturing a cache result.

### The Decision and Fixed State

The primary study begins with one architecture decision rather than an AI
method. The system goal is the 3\ W XR compute subsystem introduced in
@sec-moonshot. The local question asks which, if either, of two larger L2
capacities should advance to RTL evaluation against the current smaller
capacity. The represented study is `XR-L2-CAP-A`. Its declared cache plan fixes
the comparison against the 2\ MiB baseline, design revision `XR-COMPUTE-A`, and
run specification `RUN-SPEC-A`.

The candidate identities are `L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, and `L2-4M-A`.
`L2-2M-A` is the specified baseline, while `L2-3M-A` and `L2-4M-A` are the
specified alternatives. These names identify objects in the prospective
study. They are not retained cache configurations, generated instances, or
measured artifacts in this repository.

The represented field `l2.capacity` admits exactly the tokens `2MiB`, `3MiB`,
and `4MiB`. Those tokens identify the three specification choices and their
byte unit.

`l2.capacity` is the only swept architecture field, but it cannot be the only
serialized request value allowed to differ. Capacity may determine set count,
bank count, or SRAM macro composition. Before dispatch, a
capacity-to-implementation rule must bind those derived choices while
controlling associativity, line size, indexing, replacement, miss status
holding register (MSHR) count, ports, hit-latency allocation, and process,
voltage, and temperature assumptions. The plan declares cache policy
`CACHE-POLICY-A` and `PVT-A` as fixed across candidates, but the repository
supplies neither their bound field values nor the derivation rule. Those
unresolved policy and capacity-derived choices block dispatch.

The plan also fixes network-on-chip configuration `NOC-A`, memory-system
configuration `MEMSYS-A`, the 2\ GHz microarchitecture, compiler `COMPILER-A`,
runtime `RUNTIME-A`, RISC-V software image `SW-BASE-A`, and workload snapshot
`XR-TRACE-A` with stable frame identifiers and boundaries. It fixes the
identities of the planned cycle-level simulator `SIM-A`, cache model `CACHE-A`,
power model `PM-A`, and SRAM model `SRAM-A`.

The architecture claim is that a larger L2 could reduce 99th-percentile frame
time by removing capacity misses while satisfying the declared power, area,
access-time, functional, and coherence checks. A reduction in misses alone
would not establish the claim. The matched frame observations would have to
show that the reduction reaches the tail-latency outcome under the fixed
workload and software state.

The legal set contains only the baseline and two alternatives. Direct
evaluation was therefore selected in @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization.
The prospective study adds no generator, predictor, optimizer, or learned
search method. `SRAM-A` is part of the declared tool path, not a newly selected
AI component. This choice leaves no AI-contribution claim to test in the cache
study. It simply chooses the smallest approach that could answer the declared
architecture question if the tool path existed.

The intended result is also narrow. The study could recommend at most one
capacity for a later RTL study. It could not authorize implementation,
signoff, tapeout, or a product commitment. Cache policy, prefetching,
coherence, network-on-chip changes, compiler changes, software scheduling,
full floorplanning, thermal signoff, resistive voltage-drop review, security,
reliability, and product cost remain outside the study.

### The Run Declaration and Remaining Work

The compact request in @tbl-cache-run-declaration gathers the intended tool
roles, returns, checks, call-count limits, and stopping conditions without
treating any of them as completed. It is detailed enough to expose the work still required
before a run, but it is not an executable request.

| **Run field** | **Declared `XR-L2-CAP-A` work** |
| --- | --- |
| **Candidate requests** | Prepare one complete `SRAM-A` request under `PVT-A` for each of `L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, and `L2-4M-A`. Treat `l2.capacity` as the only swept architecture field. Hold associativity, line size, indexing, replacement, MSHR count, ports, hit-latency allocation, and PVT fixed. A prospectively bound rule may derive set count, bank count, geometry, modeled periphery, and SRAM macro composition from capacity. Retain every controlled and derived value with the SRAM-model and technology identities. The repository contains no such bindings, so these requests are unfinished. |
| **Cycle-level requests** | Rerun the `L2-2M-A` baseline and run eligible alternatives through `SIM-A` with `CACHE-A` and `PM-A` under the same `XR-TRACE-A`, `SW-BASE-A`, and fixed hardware and software identities. |
| **Dispatch condition** | No request is eligible until the controlled policy fields and all capacity-derived set, bank, geometry, periphery, and macro choices are bound. A cycle-level request is then eligible only when `(return_complete == true) && (schema_valid == true) && (area_mm2 <= 1.5) && (access_time_ns <= 2.5)`. This condition authorizes a request. It does not by itself validate a measurement or reject an architecture candidate. |
| **Required returns** | Retain SRAM area, access time, cache-local energy and leakage, matched frame records and frame-time inputs, 99th-percentile frame time, cache misses by classification, subsystem dynamic plus leakage power, tool and model identities, translated inputs, warnings, failures, hashes, lineage, and accounting records for queue and run time, compute use, license and tool use, retained storage, and human setup and review. The procedure that produces these cost records is not yet defined. |
| **Checks** | Require identical ISA-visible outputs for the declared tests, the same functional regression suite for every capacity, no failure from the simulator's coherence-invariant checks, modeled subsystem dynamic plus leakage power at or below 3\ W, cache macro area at or below 1.5\ mm^2^, modeled access time at or below 2.5\ ns, and an uncertainty-qualified frame-time comparison against the rerun baseline. Thermal and IR-drop review remain independent later requirements. |
| **Failure handling** | Refuse an invalid request before invocation. Keep timeouts, cancellations, infrastructure failures, stale state, missing output, and parser failures distinct. An authorized retry must link to its parent, consume the cycle-level budget, and begin from regenerated clean state without changing the candidate. |
| **Budget** | Allow three SRAM evaluations and at most four cycle-level executions in total, including infrastructure reruns. No RTL synthesis or physical signoff is included. Before execution, define how the study accounts for queue and run time, compute use, license and tool use, retained storage, and human setup and review, including the records or tool returns that supply each cost. This accounting procedure is unfinished. |
| **Stopping** | Stop an attempt when its queue-wait or run-time deadline expires. Stop the study when the intended decision is resolved, all eligible capacities are exhausted, the cycle-level budget is spent, the absolute deadline expires, a required input or tool remains unavailable, or no alternative passes the SRAM limits. The numeric queue-wait, run-time, and absolute deadlines remain undefined pre-execution work and block dispatch. |
| **Decision** | The direction rule requires an uncertainty-qualified frame-time improvement greater than zero. Before execution, define the estimator, interval or confidence procedure, and any additional practical margin prospectively. Once those are fixed, recommend at most one capacity for later RTL evaluation only when its required checks pass and its qualified comparison against the rerun baseline shows the declared improvement. |

: **The declaration exposes what blocks the cache run.** It identifies the
intended requests, returns, checks, call-count limits, and decision while
leaving cache-policy and derived-structure bindings, the statistical procedure,
cost accounting, numeric deadlines, and the executable measurement path
unfinished.
{#tbl-cache-run-declaration tbl-colwidths="[22,78]"}

The required direction is already fixed. Baseline latency minus candidate
latency must be qualified above zero. The unspecified details are the estimator,
the interval or confidence procedure, and any practical margin beyond zero.
They must be fixed before dispatch so that the team cannot choose an
interpretation after seeing the returns. The call-count limits likewise do not
complete the budget. The cost-accounting procedure and numeric queue-wait,
run-time, and absolute deadlines remain unfinished pre-execution work.

The placeholder names in the declaration preserve study roles and identities.
The repository does not bind `SRAM-A`, `SIM-A`, `CACHE-A`, or `PM-A` to an
installed tool, executable, configuration, or retained output. Mapping those
names to familiar cache, simulator, or power tools would invent an
implementation path that the study does not retain.

All declared capacities and serialized values use mebibytes (MiB), where
1\ MiB is $2^{20}$ bytes [@NISTBinaryPrefixes]. The candidate identities remain
stable specification names. An executable request must carry the declared MiB
token and byte count into every dependent request before comparison begins.

Nothing in @tbl-cache-run-declaration was materialized or executed for this
book. No functional regression, coherence check, tail-latency comparison,
power check, area check, access-time check, thermal review, or IR-drop review
produced cache evidence.

## Why the Cache Study Stops Before Execution

A missing implementation path does not erase the study definition, but it
changes what the record can support. The remaining work is to classify what
was retained, issue separate judgments about the unresolved decision, and
name the prerequisites for a possible new execution. That sequence prevents a detailed
plan from being mistaken for an experiment.

### What the Repository Retains

The cache material falls into three evidence classes. Specification identities
state what a study intends to compare. Author-constructed teaching records
show what an execution record could look like. Executed evidence would require
retained requests, outputs, statuses, and lineage from an actual run. The
repository retains the first two classes and no executed cache evidence.

The compact inventory in @tbl-cache-evidence-inventory keeps those classes
separate.

| **Retained item** | **Evidence class** | **What it supports** | **What remains absent** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `XR-L2-CAP-A`, `XR-COMPUTE-A`, controlled-state identifiers, and the three cache candidates | Specification identity | The cache question, comparator, intended controlled state, permitted capacity change, required measurements, call-count limits, stopping categories, and intended pre-RTL decision. | Bound policy fields, capacity-derived cache structure, retained candidate artifacts, executable requests, runs, measurements, and a cache disposition. |
| `RUN-SPEC-A` and its placeholder tool identities | Specification identity | The intended request translation, dispatch condition, return schema, failure handling, call-count limits, and tool responsibilities. | Numeric deadlines, a cost-accounting procedure, bound executables, wrapper and parser versions, exact inputs, host state, commands, logs, outputs, and realized cost. |
| Constructed SRAM and simulator entries plus the design-loop card in @fig-filled-design-loop-card | Author-constructed teaching fixture | Illustrative area, access-time, power, failure, return, and summary fields that a study record might retain. | Terminal and parser status, exact requests, raw artifacts, state identities, dispatch evidence, lineage, realized cost, and any measured cache result. |
| Retained cache execution package | Executed evidence | None. No such package is present. | Candidate artifacts, tool requests, raw outputs, parsed measurements, hashes, lineage, costs, qualified comparisons, and a decision record. |

: **The repository retains a cache specification and teaching fixtures, not a
cache experiment.** Similar-looking identifiers across chapters do not convert
constructed entries into executed evidence. {#tbl-cache-evidence-inventory tbl-colwidths="[22,18,28,32]"}

The constructed values teach how missing fields remain visible. They do not
show that a request ran or that any candidate was measured, rejected, or
advanced. In particular, the absent 4\ MiB request does not prove that a dispatch
check rejected `L2-4M-A`, and the illustrative values for `L2-3M-A` do not
establish feasibility, performance, or compliance with the 3\ W limit. The
baseline entry also does not show that `L2-2M-A` was rerun under matched
conditions.

The candidate and tool names therefore remain specification identities. They
should not be searched for as if they named retained cache files, and familiar
real tools should not be substituted for the placeholders. The absent
implementation, measurement, and dispatch prerequisites control the current
stop.

### Four Judgments and the Next Action

A study that stops before execution still needs separate judgments. The four
judgments in @tbl-cache-judgments prevent an empty run from acquiring a result
through narrative completion.

| **Judgment** | **Cache conclusion** | **Evidence boundary** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Architecture outcome** | Unresolved. No capacity advances, and none is rejected. | No retained cache candidate was executed, the baseline was not rerun, and no required comparison was qualified. |
| **AI contribution** | Not tested. | Direct evaluation with no added learned method was the declared approach. No AI-versus-conventional comparison exists. |
| **Mechanism** | Untested. | No retained miss classifications or matched frame observations test whether reduced capacity misses change 99th-percentile frame time. |
| **Stopping** | Stop before execution because the implementation, measurement, and dispatch prerequisites are unavailable. | The declared budget was not consumed. If the cache decision remains worth pursuing, a new run requires bound policy and derived cache choices, numeric deadlines, a cost-accounting procedure, candidate artifacts, tool bindings, request translation, and an executable measurement path. Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. |

: **The cache decision remains open for four different reasons.** Missing
execution leaves the architecture outcome unresolved, the declared no-added-method
choice leaves AI contribution untested, missing observations leave the mechanism
untested, and absent execution prerequisites fix the stopping point. {#tbl-cache-judgments tbl-colwidths="[18,34,48]"}

The stop belongs before execution. It is not a budget exhaustion, a failed
candidate, or a no-change architecture result. It does not authorize
`L2-2M-A`, `L2-3M-A`, or `L2-4M-A` for RTL work. If the cache decision remains
worth pursuing, continuation requires a new run whose retained package contains
the bound policy and derived cache choices, numeric deadlines, cost-accounting
procedure, exact candidate artifacts, bound tools, translated inputs, raw and
parsed returns, realized costs, qualified comparison, and accountable decision.
Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation are also supported responses to the
unresolved study.

## A Separate Executed Array Study {#sec-executed-scale-study}

The cache record shows where a loop must stop before execution. A separate
systolic-array study shows what the loop does once tools return measurements.
The returned measurements are interpreted together to support four judgments
and a next action. The individual simulator returns do not each trigger an
architecture change.

### The Frozen Array Comparison

The retained study is named
`arch2_scale_ai_study_v1`. The [tagged v0.1.7 package](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/tree/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study)
retains its preregistration, model and execution provenance, results, and
manifest. Preregistration fixes a study's question, comparison, and
interpretation rules before results are observed, so an observed outcome
cannot retroactively change the test [@NosekEtAl2018Preregistration]. For this
architecture study, the frozen items include the legal array shapes, score,
budget, rejection checks, mechanism contrast, and decision boundary. The
study evaluates systolic-array shapes for three
synthetic general matrix multiplication (GEMM) layers. A GEMM multiplies an
$M \times K$ activation matrix by a $K \times N$ weight matrix to produce an
$M \times N$ output matrix. The three recorded $(M, N, K)$ dimension tuples
are 128 by 128 by 256, 64 by 192 by 128, and 32 by 128 by 192. The
local architecture purpose is to compare systolic-array geometries under one
fixed workload and simulator configuration. The layers are not traces from an
identified spatial-tracking pipeline or a complete XR application.

The operating sequence appears in @fig-array-study-workflow. The study freezes
its question, legal space, score, budget, and checks before the model and fixed
heuristic propose candidates. A schema rejection returns only the request to
interface repair; it does not reopen the architecture question or change the
candidate study. The repaired request then proceeds through validation and
execution. The runner allocates the same number of simulator events to both
proposal arms and retains the order, returns, and available cost fields.
Interpretation considers those returns together, separates measured results
from the proposed explanation, identifies the missing comparator and metric,
and ends with four judgments about the retained study.

![**A design loop produces several judgments, not one verdict.** The retained array study freezes the plan, selects candidates, validates the request, executes and records simulator events, and interprets the resulting record. A rejected schema returns to request repair without changing the frozen study or candidates. Interpretation then supports four separate judgments about the architecture outcome, the study-local AI contribution, the proposed mechanism, and where to stop.](images/ch8_design_loop_workflow){#fig-array-study-workflow width="100%" fig-alt="An architecture workflow freezes a plan, selects model and heuristic candidates, validates the request, executes and records simulations, and interprets the record. A schema rejection returns to request repair without changing the study. Interpretation branches to separate boxes for architecture outcome, AI contribution, mechanism status, and stopping."}

For this systolic-array decision, repairing the schema preserved a frozen
allocation of four model-arm, four heuristic-arm, and four mechanism-probe
SCALE-Sim events. The model and heuristic events ended in a score tie, while
the mechanism-probe events failed to reverse the 16 by 64 versus 64 by 16
ordering. The repaired interface enabled execution, but it did not justify an
array change or the proposed mapping explanation.

SCALE-Sim is a configurable cycle-accurate simulator for systolic accelerators;
its published design supports several dataflows and system-analysis options
[@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The retained run uses only a specific subset. It
changes array height and width under SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 with weight-stationary
dataflow, 128\ KiB for each of the three SRAMs, and configured interface
bandwidth values of 64. Those exact choices come from the package's
[frozen preregistration](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/context/pre_registration.yaml)
and retained per-run configurations, not from the simulator paper.
Weight-stationary execution keeps weight tiles at processing elements while
activation values move through the array and partial sums accumulate, reducing
repeated weight movement [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The retained protocol uses a
1,024-processing-element legality limit, a
90,000-cycle cutoff, a mandatory 32 by 32 baseline, four simulator evaluation
events per proposal arm, and four shared mechanism-probe events. The retained
protocol records an 800\ MHz clock for optional derived latency. No chapter
judgment uses that clock. The chapter's judgments use cycles.

The fixed heuristic is the budget-matched method comparator for the frozen
study. Exhaustive enumeration would instead provide a full-space reference for
the fifteen-shape legal space, at greater simulator cost than either four-event
proposal arm. Its absence limits coverage, but it cannot be added
retroactively.

The local lower-is-better score is

$$
S = \frac{\text{total cycles}}
         {\text{average layer utilization}/100}.
$$

The runner computes this score from retained SCALE-Sim outputs. It is not a
physical measurement, an area-delay product, or a universal accelerator
metric. The runner sums the `Total Cycles` column and excludes the separate
prefetch-inclusive column. Average layer utilization is the arithmetic mean of
the three per-layer SCALE-Sim `Overall Util %` values, not `Compute Util %`, so
each layer has equal weight. The score does not explicitly price
processing-element count, area, or modeled memory traffic.

The retained records also show how the comparison was constructed. Both arms
receive the same three-row CSV workload, which records a layer name and the M,
N, and K dimensions for each dense GEMM. Array rows and columns must come from
the set 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128, their product must not exceed 1,024 processing
elements, and the runner inserts the mandatory 32 by 32 baseline. Every
candidate runs under the same workload, layout, SCALE-Sim configuration,
dataflow, SRAM capacities, bandwidth fields, deadline, checks, and local
score.

The model's permitted role is equally narrow. It may return three unique legal
nonbaseline shapes and a mechanism hypothesis. It cannot invoke SCALE-Sim,
waive a check, choose the recommendation, or make the architecture decision.
The deterministic heuristic excludes the baseline and orders every legal
shape first by decreasing processing-element count, then by the absolute
log2 distance between the shape's columns-to-rows ratio and the aggregate
workload N-to-M ratio, and finally by increasing row count and column count.
It selects the first three shapes in that order.

The inserted baseline gives each proposal arm four simulator events. This is
equal simulator-event allocation, not equal total effort. The study does not
equate those events with model inference, prompt development, heuristic
construction, human setup, or review cost.

The four judgments in @fig-array-study-workflow cannot substitute for one
another. A tied architecture ranking does not show that the model and
heuristic required equal total effort. A failed mechanism prediction does not
invalidate the measured ranking, and a local ranking does not authorize a
broader architecture change. Stopping states what the retained results justify
doing next; it does not repair the other three conclusions.

### The Retained Chronology

The actual record contains one setup failure before inference, one valid model
call, and twelve successful simulator evaluation records. The chronology in
@tbl-array-chronology reports only fields retained in the package.

| **Recorded event** | **Action and return** | **Retained support and limit** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Freeze, 2026-07-14 18:19:48 UTC** | The preregistration records the workload, legal shapes, heuristic candidates, score, margin, budgets, rejection checks, mechanism contrast, and decision boundary. | An internal timestamp records this order. No external timestamp or commit binding independently proves precedence. |
| **Rejected schema request, 18:21:00 UTC** | The response-format service rejects the original JSON Schema, the machine-readable contract for structured JSON output, before inference because two constant-string properties lack explicit types. No model output or usage is produced. | The old and new schema hashes and a prose error description are retained. The rejected schema body and service response are not retained, so semantic equivalence of the amendment cannot be independently checked. |
| **Schema amendment, 18:21:41 UTC** | The record adds explicit types and marks the change non-substantive. | The package records the amendment before inference but does not retain both schema bodies. |
| **Proposal call, 18:21:51–18:22:24 UTC** | One valid call returns 16 by 64, 8 by 128, and 32 by 16 plus a directional mechanism prediction. No repair call follows. | The full response, 32.90 seconds of wall time, and token usage are retained. Provider revision, seed, temperature, top-p, host runtime, currency cost, and an exact matching prompt copy are unavailable. |
| **Simulator window, 18:31:23–18:31:42 UTC** | The record contains eight proposal-arm evaluation events and four shared mechanism-probe events. All twelve carry `status: ok`; every recorded shape satisfies the 1,024-processing-element legality limit and every result remains below the 90,000-cycle cutoff. | The aggregate runner window is 19.05 seconds. Per-evaluation timestamps, commands, exit codes, logs, queue time, resource use, and human effort are not retained. No invalid-candidate, rejection, timeout, retry, or simulator-recovery path is exercised. |
| **Technical stop and handoff** | No evaluated nonbaseline shape clears the one-percent margin. The proposal arms tie, and the predicted winner reversal fails. | The machine-readable recommendation retains 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and stops the recorded search. Its accountable decision status remains `awaiting_author_confirmation`. |

: **The array chronology records what happened and what is missing.** One
schema setup failure precedes a valid model call, twelve simulator events
complete, but no authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded.
{#tbl-array-chronology tbl-colwidths="[20,40,40]"}

The schema rejection sends the work back to request translation and interface
validation, not to the architecture question, legal shape set, score, or
evaluation budget. The amendment repairs and revalidates the response schema
while preserving the frozen study and candidate-selection procedures. Only
then does the valid proposal call proceed to simulation. This is a request
repair within the retained study, not a new architecture iteration.

The model provenance names OpenAI through Codex CLI 0.144.4 and the requested
alias `gpt-5.4`. It records 13,223 input tokens, including 1,920 cached tokens,
and 1,446 output tokens, including 516 reasoning tokens. Currency cost was not
reported. The exact hosted model revision and sampling identity[^fn-sampling-identity-c08] were not
exposed, so another call cannot be treated as reproduction of this one.

[^fn-sampling-identity-c08]: **Sampling identity**: A random seed and decoding settings such as temperature and top-p can change the generated tokens. Recording them narrows one source of run-to-run variation, but it cannot make a hosted call exactly reproducible when the provider's model revision or serving state is unavailable.

The retained prompt has a second provenance break. The preregistration and
model record name SHA-256 `ec12df200a134532...76fbca`, while the surviving
prompt copy hashes to `36e0167aa338c6b...6971`. The complete response survives,
but the exact context that produced it cannot be verified.

The simulator provenance records macOS 26.4 on arm64, Python 3.11.15,
`arch2_labs` 0.1.0, SCALE-Sim 3.0.0, and a local executable path. It does not
bind the historical runner to a repository commit, dependency lock,
container, or complete host state. The reference manifest covers the retained
reference-output tree, not the preregistration, prompt, model response,
provenance record, runner source, dependency lock, or repository commit as one
sealed identity.

The retained array directory contains no independently preserved validation
receipt artifact. This chapter therefore does not treat reference integrity,
replay, or focused tests as independently verified. The retained files and
current replay path remain inspectable, but replay would still share the
workload, runner, simulator, score, and assumptions of the recorded
computation. The executed record contains no study-local independent analytical,
RTL, or cross-simulator check. No analytical fold-count sanity check ran. A
newly frozen mechanism study could add that check as future work, but the
mapping discussion below is the author's interpretation of the tagged simulator
implementation, not executed evidence.

### The Local Results

The model arm evaluates the mandatory baseline plus its three proposals. The
fixed aggregate-aspect-ratio heuristic evaluates the same baseline plus 16 by
64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16. The two arms overlap on two nonbaseline shapes.
Including the repeated baseline, both arms receive four simulator evaluation
events. That equality does not match model inference, human setup, heuristic
construction, prompt development, review effort, or total cost.

The exact proposal-arm results appear in @tbl-array-results. Repeated rows are
separate budget events, not independent measurements.

| **Arm** | **Shape and source** | **PE count (author-derived)** | **Cycles** | **Average layer utilization** | **Local score** | **Result within arm** |

| Heuristic | 16 by 64 proposal | `{python} f"{16 * 64:,}"` | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 8 by 128 proposal | `{python} f"{8 * 128:,}"` | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 64 by 16 proposal | `{python} f"{64 * 16:,}"` | 17,757 | 32.294% | 54,985.25 | Ranked worse |

: **The two proposal arms tie under equal simulator-event budgets.** Neither
finds an evaluated nonbaseline shape that clears the recorded one-percent
margin over 32 by 32. The values come from retained SCALE-Sim outputs and the
runner's local score, not silicon. PE counts are author-derived from rows times
columns. {#tbl-array-results tbl-colwidths="[10,19,12,10,16,13,20]"}

The 32 by 16 proposal contains `{python} f"{32 * 16:,}"` processing elements,
while 32 by 32, 16 by 64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16 each contain
`{python} f"{32 * 32:,}"`. Shape and processing-element count therefore vary
together in the 32 by 16 comparison. A design with
`{python} f"{32 * 16:,}"` processing elements may have a different resource
tradeoff from the relevant shapes with `{python} f"{32 * 32:,}"` processing
elements, but this study measured no area or energy consequence of that
difference. The retained result remains a score-only local outcome.

The best evaluated nonbaseline, 16 by 64, exactly matches the baseline on
cycles, average layer utilization, and local score. It does not clear the
change margin. The 8 by 128, 32 by 16, and 64 by 16 results rank worse under
the frozen score. This is a no-change outcome for five unique evaluated
shapes. It is not evidence that 32 by 32 is optimal among all legal shapes.

@fig-ai-study-result separates the proposal ranking from the mechanism test so
that a tied score cannot be read as support for the directional explanation.

The tie provides no study-local AI advantage over the fixed heuristic
under equal simulator-event budgets. It also provides no evidence of equal
capability, equal total cost, or parity with exhaustive enumeration, an expert
study, a solver, or another search method. One proposal call supplies no estimate
of variation or reliability for the model family.

The retained results establish equal cycles and average layer utilization for
32 by 32 and 16 by 64 under the frozen score, but they do not establish the
architectural cause of that equality. The following transposition probe tests
a separate mechanism hypothesis by comparing 16 by 64 with 64 by 16.

### The Failed Directional Explanation

The model predicted that 16 by 64 would beat 64 by 16 on the original workload
and that 64 by 16 would win after M and N were exchanged. The original local
scores are 33,782.40 and 54,985.25. The transposed scores are 23,530.65 and
25,458.11. The predicted reversal does not occur. The narrower transposed gap
does not rescue the explanation.

Separately, the retained report exposes an unresolved simulator-semantics
issue that neither explains nor rescues the failed reversal. The transposed 16
by 64 input config declares `Bandwidth = 64,64,64`, while one retained report
row gives `Avg OFMAP DRAM BW` as 79.073. The retained record does not explain
the relationship between those fields. Their bandwidth semantics remain
unresolved, and the configured value is not evidence of a demonstrated
physical or shared-system limit.

The surviving prompt copy also omits the mapping semantics needed to interpret
the contrast. The retained execution records identify SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 but no
dependency hash or source commit. The K-height, N-width, and M-temporal
interpretation here follows the tagged v3.0.0 implementation
[@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source]. Under SCALE-Sim's weight-stationary GEMM
mode, K maps across the array height, N maps across its width, and M advances
over time rather than occupying a spatial array dimension
(@fig-array-mapping). A fold count is the number of array-sized passes needed
to cover a mapped workload dimension, such as $\lceil K/\text{height}\rceil$
or $\lceil N/\text{width}\rceil$. Exchanging M and N changes the temporal
extent and the width-mapped dimension while leaving K unchanged. Mirroring 16
by 64 and 64 by 16 simultaneously changes both the N-fold count on width and
the K-fold count on height, so the probe does not isolate array orientation.

![**The retained contrast does not isolate array orientation.** In the tagged SCALE-Sim v3.0.0 implementation [@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source], weight-stationary GEMM maps K to array height and N to array width, while M streams through the array. Exchanging M and N leaves K unchanged, so the mirrored shapes change more than one fold count.](images/F8-array-mapping){#fig-array-mapping fig-alt="A GEMM workload feeds a resident weight tile of K by N, which maps onto wide 16 by 64 and tall 64 by 16 arrays. K maps over array height and N over array width. A dashed transpose connector notes that K is unchanged, so the mirrored pair changes more than one fold count."}

The directional prediction fails its declared test, but the contrast does not
establish a replacement mechanism. It does not show that orientation is
irrelevant. A new mechanism study would need a prompt with pinned mapping
semantics and a contrast that varies one relevant fold count at a time.

The retained array record therefore ends with four separate judgments. No
evaluated nonbaseline clears the architecture margin. The study demonstrates
no study-local AI advantage over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event
budgets. The directional explanation fails without yielding a replacement. The
technical search stops, but no authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded.

The retained SCALE-Sim configuration and outputs establish none of the
physical properties that the Lighthouse decision needs. This run preserves no
energy, physical bandwidth, timing, power, area, thermal, or silicon result,
even though the broader SCALE-Sim v3 tool supports additional memory, energy,
and power analyses [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The configured bandwidth fields
and reported operand traffic do not describe a verified shared-system
interface. The synthetic workload and local array result cannot close the
cache decision, the 3\ W requirement, or the Lighthouse system.

## Coverage, Proxy Limits, and a Follow-up Study

The array study's legal space is small and closed. It contains exactly fifteen
shapes under the declared dimension set and 1,024-processing-element limit.
The retained proposal-arm evaluations cover five unique shapes, leaving ten
unexecuted. The exact coverage appears in @tbl-array-shape-coverage.

| **Status** | **Exact legal shapes** | **Count** |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Evaluated as unique original-workload geometries | 8 by 128; 16 by 64; 32 by 16; 32 by 32; 64 by 16 | 5 |
| Not executed | 8 by 8; 8 by 16; 8 by 32; 8 by 64; 16 by 8; 16 by 16; 16 by 32; 32 by 8; 64 by 8; 128 by 8 | 10 |

: **Five evaluated geometries do not close a fifteen-shape space.** Repeated
arm events preserve the frozen budgets but add no new geometry. The ten other
legal shapes have no retained SCALE-Sim result. {#tbl-array-shape-coverage tbl-colwidths="[25,62,13]"}

For a newly frozen follow-up study, exhaustive enumeration would provide a
full-space reference by evaluating every legal shape under one fixed workload,
simulator configuration, score, and set of checks. It is not budget-matched to
the current four-event proposal arms. A follow-up must either budget its greater
simulator cost explicitly or use it only as a coverage baseline. The current
study did not perform that enumeration. No outcome for the ten unexecuted shapes
can be inferred, and enumeration cannot be added retroactively to claim that
the recorded model tied or beat the complete space.

The frozen score also omits a reported axis that could matter to a later
system decision. The 16 by 64 shape ties the baseline at 13,917 cycles and
41.196 percent average layer utilization, yet the retained reports contain
409,726 modeled DRAM writes for 16 by 64 and 204,863 for 32 by 32. The
64 by 16 shape reports 102,400 modeled writes and fewer total modeled accesses
than the baseline while taking more cycles. These are simulator outputs, not
identified physical DRAM transactions or energy measurements.

The baseline dominates the shared 16 by 64 candidate on the two reported
quantities of cycles and modeled writes (@fig-proxy-mismatch). This post-run
observation exposes a proxy limitation. It does not change the frozen score,
establish physical memory energy, or authorize a new disposition.

```{python}
#| label: fig-proxy-mismatch
#| fig-cap: |
#|   **The frozen score omits modeled memory traffic.** The local score ranks the shared 16 by 64 candidate exactly equal to the 32 by 32 baseline. Across cycles and modeled DRAM writes, the baseline dominates that candidate. This post-run observation does not change the frozen outcome or establish physical memory energy.
#| out-width: "80%"

import json
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from _python.plots import COLORS, apply_style

apply_style()

result_path = Path("../labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json")
result = json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
arm_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] in {"model", "conventional"}]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.5))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.18, right=0.95, top=0.95, bottom=0.15)

ax.set_xlabel("SCALE-Sim total cycles (lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)
ax.set_ylabel("Modeled DRAM writes (lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)

seen = set()
for r in arm_runs:
    key = (r["workload_id"], r["array_rows"], r["array_cols"])
    if key in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(key)

    cid = r["candidate_id"]

    if "32x32" in label:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="o", markersize=5, color=COLORS["blue"])
        ax.text(cycles - 500, dram_writes - 10000, f"Baseline\n{label}", color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5.5, ha="right", va="top")
    elif "16x64" in label:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="X", markersize=5, color=COLORS["red"])
        ax.text(cycles + 300, dram_writes + 15000, f"Shared candidate\n{label}", color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5.5, ha="left", va="bottom")
    else:

ax.grid(True, color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=0.55, zorder=0)
for spine in ["top", "right"]:
```

A new enumeration study would need to freeze its decision quantities before
execution. It could retain the original local score for comparability, add a
separately justified memory-aware quantity, or replace the score. None of
those choices can rescore the retained executed study. The unresolved memory
axis is part of the reason that neither exhaustive coverage nor the current
local ranking alone would establish energy, power, or Lighthouse suitability.

The executed record changes how the next study should be run. The recorded
ranking tied, the directional explanation failed, and modeled memory traffic
was missing from the frozen score. A follow-up should therefore budget a
full-space reference separately, revise the metric prospectively rather than
rescore this record, and isolate one proposed mechanism at a time.

## Two Stops and Their Next Actions

The comparison in @tbl-lighthouse-return places the two stopping points side by
side.

| **Record** | **Architecture outcome** | **AI contribution** | **Mechanism** | **Stopping and action** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prospective cache study `XR-L2-CAP-A` | Unresolved. No cache candidate was evaluated, rejected, or advanced. | Not tested because direct evaluation with no added learned method was selected. | Untested. No retained result connects capacity misses to 99th-percentile frame time. | Stop before execution because the cache implementation, measurement, and dispatch prerequisites are unavailable. If the decision remains worth pursuing, continuation requires a new fully retained run with the missing bindings, procedures, and artifacts. Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. |
| Executed array study `arch2_scale_ai_study_v1` | No evaluated nonbaseline clears the local margin for five unique shapes. This is not an optimality result. | No study-local advantage is demonstrated over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event budgets. Equal total cost and method parity were not measured. | The directional reversal prediction fails, and no replacement explanation is established. | The machine-readable recommendation is to retain 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and stop the local technical search. No authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded. |

: **The two records stop at different technical boundaries.** The cache study
never executes, while the retained array study executes a narrow simulator
comparison for which no authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded.
Neither result can close the other.
{#tbl-lighthouse-return tbl-colwidths="[19,22,20,18,21]"}

The executed case shows how a returned signal affects a claim, supports a
judgment, and determines whether the next action belongs to the current record
or to a newly frozen study.

- **Tie.** The returned scores affect the claim that the model-guided proposals
  improve the local architecture result. They support no study-local advantage
  over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event budgets, so the current
  record retains 32 by 32 for the evaluated set. Testing a broader selection
  claim requires a newly frozen, separately budgeted full-space reference.
- **Failed mechanism.** The transposition results affect the directional
  explanation, not the measured ranking. They reject the predicted reversal
  without establishing a replacement mechanism. Isolating that mechanism
  requires a newly frozen study with pinned mapping semantics.
- **Omitted metric.** The modeled traffic counts expose a quantity absent from
  the frozen score. They do not change the current ranking or permit post-run
  rescoring. Any memory-aware decision quantity belongs in a newly frozen
  study.
- **Provenance gap.** The missing prompt identity and incomplete simulator
  provenance limit a reproduction claim. The current record remains usable
  within those limits. A new run must retain the exact prompt, model revision
  when available, runner revision, dependencies, commands, and complete
  outputs.
- **Pending authority.** The machine-readable technical recommendation retains
  32 by 32 for the evaluated set, but no authorized acceptance or rejection
  was recorded. The next action within the current record is review, not an
  architecture commitment.

The tie, failed mechanism, omitted metric, and provenance gap identify four
possible follow-up studies. None of those studies ran as part of the retained
execution. They must be declared and frozen separately. Even if run, they
would not establish XR behavior or the 3\ W system target because those
conclusions require system checks absent from the retained configuration and
outputs.

Both records leave the central system questions open. Neither retains an
identified XR workload trace or validates tail deadlines across deployed
conditions. Neither executes the compiler, runtime, RISC-V interface, host
cores, shared memory path, sensors, or display engine. Neither supplies a
complete verification plan or checks the full subsystem's function, security,
or reliability.

The physical questions also remain. No retained evidence closes timing,
routing, area, power delivery, the 3\ W subsystem budget, thermal behavior, or
silicon performance. The array reports contain modeled local traffic, but no
shared-memory contention or physical energy model connects that traffic to the
Lighthouse platform. The cache plan names some of these checks, but naming a
check is not running it.

The supported dispositions are therefore plain. The cache architecture decision
is unresolved. The array study reaches a local technical stop and demonstrates
no study-local AI advantage over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event
budgets. No authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded, and no architecture
commitment was made. Neither case is a complete Lighthouse success.

## Open Research Questions

These records leave open three problems about operating an AI-assisted
architecture study when the intended comparison may not execute, distinguish
the proposal methods, or remain valid after the experiment plan changes. The
questions move from readiness for one run to the validity of an adaptive loop.

**Determining readiness before dispatch.** A coherent architecture question
does not ensure that the intended comparison can run or support its declared
decision.

- **Can an AI-assisted architecture system determine before dispatch whether
  its candidate artifacts, tool path, measurement procedure, and decision rule
  are complete enough to execute the intended architecture comparison?** A
  first experiment could seed realistic omissions into a corpus of architecture
  studies and measure which incomplete plans the system detects and which valid
  plans it falsely rejects. The technical difficulty is recognizing omissions
  that appear only through interactions among otherwise plausible study parts
  without reducing readiness to a fixed checklist.

**Testing whether a comparison can decide.** Even a valid run may be
uninformative if proposal methods select the same candidates or the budget
stops before their differences appear.

- **Can an AI-assisted architecture study determine before execution whether
  its candidate set and tool budget can distinguish competing proposal
  methods?** A first experiment could hide the returns from completed studies,
  predict from planned candidate sets and budgets whether each comparison will
  separate its methods, and then check those predictions against retained
  results. The technical difficulty is that overlap can erase method
  differences, while a small budget may miss the few candidates that expose
  them.

**Revising an experiment without biasing it.** Failures and interim results may
justify changing the plan, but those changes also alter which candidates and
outcomes the study observes.

- **How can an AI-assisted architecture loop revise its experiment plan after
  failures or interim results without invalidating the comparison it eventually
  reports?** A first experiment could compare adaptive and frozen plans under
  matched tool budgets and test their bias and candidate coverage. The technical
  difficulty is separating a useful response to new evidence from a change that
  steers the remaining runs toward a favorable result.

## Conclusion

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Stop at the last retained result"}
Separate the architecture outcome, AI contribution, mechanism, and stopping
decision. When execution evidence ends, leave every downstream claim open and
state the new work required to continue.
:::

The primary cache study reaches a supported stop before execution. Its exact
candidate identities, controlled-state declarations, planned requests, required
returns, checks, call-count limits, and intended pre-RTL decision survive. Its
policy bindings, capacity-derived structure, numeric deadlines, cost-accounting
procedure, implementation path, and measurement path do not. The repository
therefore supports no cache measurement, candidate rejection, retry, dispatch,
return, cost, baseline comparison, AI-contribution result, mechanism result, or
architecture recommendation.

The separate array study reaches a different stop. It retains one schema
setup failure, one valid model response with provenance gaps, twelve SCALE-Sim
evaluation events, five unique evaluated shapes, a tie against a fixed
heuristic, a failed directional explanation, an omitted memory axis, and a
technical recommendation to retain 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and stop.
No authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded. The study does not
establish array optimality, equal total cost, method parity, physical
feasibility, or any full-system XR result.

Neither record produces a win claim. If the cache decision remains worth
pursuing, a new fully retained execution requires the missing cache bindings,
numeric deadlines, cost procedure, artifacts, and measurement path. Deferral,
cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. A broader array
candidate-selection claim would require a newly frozen, separately budgeted
full-space comparison, followed by system-relevant checks that were absent from
the retained run.
The next chapter asks which parts of the executed array study and its retained
record can be reused when the workload, objective, tool, implementation target,
or system context changes
(@sec-loop-patterns-across-stack).
